_readme: THE SHARED HOSTNAME-NORMALIZER VECTOR TABLE — read by BOTH suites.
Consumers, and there must never be fewer than two:
- Go: internal/driver/hostname_vectors_test.go, over driver.HostnameFromDeviceName
- TS: web/src/pages/add/hostname_vectors.test.ts, over hostnameFromDeviceName
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. There are two implementations of one rule, in two
languages, and they must agree FOREVER: a switch provisioned from a console
(the browser scripts, TS) and the same switch reconciled by the healer (the
controller, Go) would otherwise be named two different things, and the healer
would then chase a drift it can never resolve. Until this table existed that
agreement was asserted only by two hand-written suites that happened to carry
similar cases — nothing failed when one side was edited and the other was not.
That is precisely the drift that produced the ten spellings collapsed on
2026-08-09/10, so the unification would have come undone the first time
somebody "fixed" one side.
THIS FILE LIVES UNDER web/ ON PURPOSE. `make test-web` mounts ONLY
/srv/meshcraft/web into its container, so the TS suite can read nothing outside
it; `make test-go` mounts the whole repo at /src, so the Go suite can reach
ACROSS to here. web/ is the only directory both suites can see, so the table
lives here and the Go test walks up to it.
FULL REFUSAL SENTENCES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED HERE. The Go messages in
internal/driver/hostname.go are the operator-facing authority and are asserted
word for word in the Go suite; copying them into this file would create a THIRD
place to update whenever a sentence is reworded, and a third place to forget is
how the drift started. What is pinned instead is the MARKER that carries the
meaning: the offending character the refusal must name, or the phrase that
separates one diagnosis from another — "does not shorten it" is the ceiling
refusal, "may only carry letters" is the alphabet refusal, "no meshcraft
name" is the nothing-to-derive-from refusal. A reworded sentence that still
says the same thing keeps passing; a refusal that changes its MIND fails on
both sides at once.
EVERY FIELD IS MANDATORY IN BOTH SUITES:
why              - what the vector defends, quoted back in the failure
in               - the meshcraft device name handed to the normalizer
hostname         - the expected system name; EMPTY exactly when refused
refusal_contains - substrings the refusal must carry; EMPTY when accepted
Both suites also assert the whole-table invariants: exactly one of hostname /
refusal is non-empty, and any non-empty hostname passes that language's own
ValidHostname — the string a connector concatenates into a command line.
INVISIBLE CHARACTERS ARE WRITTEN AS \u ESCAPES, never pasted literally: a
vector nobody can see in a diff is a vector nobody can review.
DO NOT ADJUST A VECTOR TO MAKE A DISAGREEMENT GO AWAY. A vector the two sides
answer differently is the finding this file was built to produce; fix the side
that is wrong. The TS module is documented as MIRRORING the Go one, so where
they genuinely differ Go is the authority — it is the path the fleet actually
converges to.

vectors.why: an already-valid name passes through untouched: normalizing is not a licence to rewrite what was already right
hyphens an operator typed themselves survive
case is NOT folded — a lowercasing normalizer on one side only would rename half the fleet on its next pass
a single character is a name
digits alone are a name
separator set: space maps to hyphen
separator set: underscore maps to hyphen — four of the five Go spellings KEPT it, which ValidHostname forbids outright
separator set: dot maps to hyphen
separator set: slash maps to hyphen
separator set: tab maps to hyphen
the whole separator set in one name — space, underscore, dot, slash, tab, and nothing else is rewritten
a run of hyphens collapses to one
a long run collapses just as far
separators of MIXED kinds collapse together, not each to its own hyphen
a run made of a separator and a typed hyphen is still one hyphen
surrounding whitespace is trimmed, not turned into edge hyphens
a leading hyphen is TRIMMED, not refused — the operator wrote a separator and meant one
a trailing hyphen is trimmed; four of the five Go spellings never trimmed and shipped the trailing hyphen RFC 1123 rejects
hyphens at BOTH ends are trimmed
a separator at the edges becomes a hyphen and is then trimmed away with it
a trailing space is trimmed before anything else happens
a trailing CR is whitespace and is trimmed — it is an injection only when it is INTERIOR
a name that is NOTHING but separators has no name left in it: empty is a refusal, never the literal `switch` all five spellings fell back to
refusal_contains: cannot be used as a system name
an empty system name is not a name

vectors.why: empty input has nothing to derive from, and says so in its own words rather than the alphabet's
whitespace-only input is empty input
whitespace-only counts tab and newline as whitespace on both sides
THE accented case: "Switch étage 1" must REFUSE, never become `Switch-tage-1` — a mangled name looks deliberate on a console banner and nothing connects it back to the deleted letter
refusal_contains: may only carry letters, digits and hyphens

vectors.why: non-ASCII refuses even with no separator in sight
an astral-plane character is named as ONE character: Go ranges over runes and TS over code points, and a UTF-16 code-unit loop would name two broken halves
three-byte characters refuse, and the offenders are named in the order met
a repeated offender is named once, not once per occurrence
U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE at the edges is whitespace to Go's TrimSpace and to JS .trim(): it is trimmed on both sides
U+000B VERTICAL TAB at the edges: whitespace to both, and NOT one of the five separators — it is trimmed away, never turned into a hyphen
U+2000 EN QUAD at the edges pins the U+2000-U+200A range of Go's White_Space set — the part of the set a hand-written mirror is most likely to forget
U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR at the edges: a line terminator to JS and White_Space to Go, so both trim it
U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE at the edges is whitespace on both sides too
U+0085 NEXT LINE is whitespace to Go's strings.TrimSpace but is NOT in JS String.prototype.trim's set — a mirror that leans on .trim() refuses here while Go accepts

U+FEFF BYTE ORDER MARK is the mirror image: JS .trim() eats it, Go's TrimSpace does not. Go refuses, and refusing is right — swallowing an invisible character silently is exactly the mangling this module exists to end. A name pasted out of a CSV export carries one.
refusal_contains: may only carry letters, digits and hyphens

vectors.why: a NO-BREAK SPACE in the MIDDLE is not one of the five separators: it refuses rather than quietly becoming a hyphen
refusal_contains: may only carry letters, digits and hyphens

vectors.why: injection: a newline would run what follows it as a SECOND configuration command with the session's privileges — refuse, do not strip the newline and send the rest
refusal_contains: may only carry letters, digits and hyphens

vectors.why: injection: an INTERIOR carriage return is a line ending on every CLI range
refusal_contains: may only carry letters, digits and hyphens

vectors.why: injection: a semicolon chains a second command on several ranges
injection: backticks substitute a command
injection: a pipe redirects into another command
injection: $(...) substitutes a command, and every one of its characters is outside the alphabet
injection: a NUL byte truncates the string inside a C-implemented CLI, so what the device stores is not what was validated
refusal_contains: may only carry letters, digits and hyphens

vectors.why: the 63-octet ceiling: 62 octets is under it and passes
the 63-octet ceiling: 63 IS the DNS label limit and is ACCEPTED — an off-by-one on either side gives one path a name the other refuses
the 63-octet ceiling: 64 REFUSES and says meshcraft will not shorten it — a truncated hostname answers to a name the inventory does not carry, and its LLDP system name stops matching

THE MOST VALUABLE VECTOR IN THIS TABLE: 32 × "é" is 32 CHARACTERS but 64 OCTETS. Go counts octets with len(); a TS mirror using .length would count 32, sail past the ceiling and hand back the ALPHABET refusal instead of this one. That visible difference in WHY is the only cheap symptom of the two sides disagreeing about HOW LONG a name may be — the same disagreement that, on an all-ASCII name, would silently rename a device.

the other side of that boundary: 31 × "é" is 62 octets, UNDER the ceiling, so the refusal must be the alphabet one and must name the character. A .length implementation cannot tell this vector from the one above; an octet-counting one always can.
refusal_contains: may only carry letters, digits and hyphens

vectors.why: three-byte characters widen the character/octet gap further: 22 × "交" is 22 characters and 66 octets, over the ceiling
vectors.in: 交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交

vectors.why: 21 × "交" is exactly 63 octets — on the ceiling, not over it — so it earns the alphabet refusal instead
vectors.in: 交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交交

vectors.why: runs collapse BEFORE the ceiling is measured: 64 separators between two letters is 66 input octets but a 3-octet name
